facts.text: J Hannon, the licensed building practitioner and agent for owners M and P Pearce, is the applicant; Dunedin City Council is the authority; the dispute concerns a new house at 99B Forfar Street, Mosgiel.
The authority treated the proposed footing detail as an alternative solution and considered it did not comply with Clause B1 of the Building Code.
The determination compares the proposed footing detail with Acceptable Solutions SH/AS1 and B1/AS1 in terms of flexural and shear capacity.
The proposed house is a single-storey timber-framed dwelling on a concrete slab with reinforced perimeter footings; brick veneer with fibre-cement weatherboard gables; corrugated steel roof.

The dispute centres on the footing detail (Figure 1, not to scale); on 16 November 2016 the authority sent a request for information noting an NZS 3604 minimum-footing requirement (text truncated in extraction).
